title: American Heritage Riverboat Capsizes in New Orleans After Tanker Strike
excerpt: The American Heritage riverboat capsized on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoon after being struck by the tanker Atlantic Asphalt, sending passengers into the water and triggering a major rescue effort.
content:
The American Heritage riverboat capsized on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoon, Nov. 13, after it was struck by the tanker Atlantic Asphalt, sending passengers into the water and triggering a major rescue operation.

The collision happened at about 12:30 p.m. Central Time, below the Crescent City Connection bridge. The Atlantic Asphalt, a Marshall Islands-flagged, 524-foot asphalt and bitumen tanker, struck the riverboat while it was docked.

About 129 passengers were aboard the American Heritage, along with crew members. The riverboat rolled onto its side, capsized and was left partially submerged in the river.

A major rescue is underway, with the U.S. Coast Guard, the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department, EMS and Port NOLA Harbor Police responding to pull people from the water.

The Mississippi River has been closed to vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96 while the rescue and response continue.

More than a dozen people have been hospitalized, according to WDSU, citing the mayor's office. No deaths have been reported at this time. The cause of the collision is under investigation. This is a developing story.

Sources: USA Today, NY Post, gCaptain and ABC News; hospitalizations reported by WDSU, citing the mayor's office. Video: TikTok @blas.armas.
